newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: BRITISH WOMAN DIES IN DIVING ACCIDENT
A nineteen-year-old British woman is dead after a diving accident
on the Great Barrier Reef off Townsville in North Queensland.
It's beleived the woman had been a research volunteer on an Australian Institute of Marine Science vessel.
The accident occurred yesterday afternoon when the woman was diving at Davies Reef 55-nautical-miles east-nor-east of Townsville.
Police say the woman was seen to break the surface in distressed state then disappeared from sight.
ARKO CLAIMS PLAYERS BEHIND ARL
Chairman of the Australian Rugby League, Ken Arthurson, says contracts with players loyal to the ARL will stand.
Mr Arthurson's urged his players to ignore advances to defect to Superleague, and claims his players are 100-per cent behind the ARL.
SUN ADMITS PHOTOS A FRAUD
The Sun newspaper in Britain says it's been the victim of one of the most elaborate hoaxes of the decade.
It's admitted that pictures it printed, allegedly showing the Princess of Wales in compromising positions, were fraudulent.
The Rupert Murdoch-owned Sun is apologising profusely to the Princess of Wales and her former lover, James Hewitt.
The Sun's editor, Stuart Higgins, says he now thinks the video was designed to embarrass him and his paper.
The Princess of Wales has issued a statement saying she didn't recognise herself or her ex-lover from the pictures.
STONE HAPPY EUTHANASIA CONTROVERSY WILL BE HEARD

Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone says while he would have prefered all debate on the Andrews' anti-euthansia bill to be in the main chamber, he's satisified any issue of controversy will be heard.
Territory M-P Nick Dondas last night supported the motion in Federal Parliament to move debate on the Andrews' bill to the secondary Chamber of the House, after the first ninety minutes.
Territory Senator Bob Collins says the move will give the bill a "dream run" through parliament.
Mr Stone says those who oppose the Andrews' bill, including a number of Coalition members, agreed to the motion on the
understanding that if there was any controversy it would all be taken in the main chamber.
SHARP LAUNCHED RENEWED PUSH ON CIVIL AVIATION AUTHORITY
Federal Transport Minister, John Sharp has renewed his push for changes to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority, following the findings of the Seaview Air crash inquiry.

The Safety agency, in its former guise as the Civil Aviation Authority, has been held partly responsible for the fatal crash of a Seaview plane two years ago through its failure to stringently enforce air safety standards.
Mr Sharp says until the Authority's directors resign, whom he says lack aviation experience, he can't assure the travelling public their safety is being adequately protected.
The Board members have rejected Mr Sharp's demand.
EXHIBITION BUILDINGS FOR WORLD HERITAGE LISTING
The Melbourne City Council last night proposed the nomination of the Royal Exhibition Buildings for World Heritage listing.
The Council's Planning and Development Committee unanimously agreed to the nomination and it's expected to be adopted at a full Council meeting later this month.
A spokesperson for the Defend Our Heritage group, Anthony van der Craats, says World Heritage listing is a long drawn out process.
WOMEN DOCTORS STILL ASKED ABOUT CHILDREN - SURVEY
A new survey has found that female doctors are still being asked by hospitals whether they plan to have children.
Professor Rosemary Pringle, from the Australian Institute for medical research and policy, has conducted a survey looking at workplace conditions for female doctors.
She says hospital boards believe they have authority to ask these questions because of the nature of a doctor's job.
TB FREE STATUS NEEDS TO BE MAINTAINED, SAYS UGA
The United Graziers Association says it's vital Australia maintains its TB free status after 1997.
The UGA is urging the Commonwealth to maintain current funding levels for tuberculosis and brucellosis eradication schemes.
The UGA's John Stewart says the Government is suggesting it won't meet its current A$6.9 million dollar contribution over the next five years.
With Australia is set to be declared TB-free at the end of 1997, Mr Stewart says monitoring needs to continue beyond that.
RABBIT VIRUS RELEASED LATER TODAY
The rabbit calici virus has its first official release today.
Farmers are counting on the virus to solve a 600 million dollar problem.

Today won't be the first time the virus has been let loose on the wild rabbit population.. it got away on the CSIRO last year, when it escaped from a South Australian test site. After intensive lobbying by farmers the virus will be released again today, but this time in New South Wales, near the town of Wagga Wagga.

Agriculture Minister, Richard Amery, says he's confident the virus won't harm people, or native fauna. But the timing of the release has prompted new concerns, given evidence that young rabbits may have some immunity to the virus.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
